veranderings.voor: dit is nou reg en dek die bak
veranderings.na: dit is nou reg, en sy dek die bak
veranderings.rede: Without its own subject the second verb can be read as belonging to 'dit' (the dough covers the bowl); giving it 'sy' makes two full clauses, which take the AWS comma before 'en'.

veranderings.voor: sodra sy die eerste paar keer druk
veranderings.na: sodra sy die deeg die eerste paar keer druk
veranderings.rede: 'Druk' has no object here, so it is unclear what she presses; naming the dough, which is already in the bowl, makes the sentence clear without adding content.

veranderings.voor: met die onderkant van sy hand diep
veranderings.na: met die onderkant van sy handpalm diep
veranderings.rede: 'Die onderkant van sy hand' is vague (it could be the side or the back of the hand); 'handpalm' names the part used for kneading.
'Dus' sounds like a logical conclusion; 'daarom' reads more naturally in a Grade 5 story and keeps the same meaning and word order.

vlae.teks: Neo haal die vier brode uit en sit hulle op die rak.
vlae.rede: The story never mentions an oven, so 'haal ... uit' says nothing about where the loaves come out of. Adding 'uit die oond' would make it clearer, but that adds a detail, so this is left for the writer to decide.
